newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Perstorp says currency moves hit profit.
newsitem.headline: Perstorp says currency moves hit profit.

text.p: Swedish chemicals and plastics company Perstorp AB on Friday said currency fluctuations reduced its profits for the year 1995/96 by 93 million crowns while weak demand from key markets also had a negative impact.
Perstorp posted a fall in pre-tax profit to 716 million crowns for the year to August 31 from 745 million crowns a year earlier.
"The business year has suffered from a downturn in the business cycle especially on European markets," the company's managing director Gosta Wiking said in statement.
The company said its series A shares, currently owned by the family of company founder Wilhelm Wendt, would be listed on the Stockholm bourse in March 1997 alongside its B shares.

"It has been concluded that a listing of the company's series A shares will increase the stock market's interest in Perstorp and thus provide conditions for increased trading in Perstorp shares," it said.
"A limited diversification of ownership of series A shares, which fulfils the Stockholm Stock Exchange's listing requirements, will be effected."
The company said it would pay a dividend of 2.50 crowns.
The dividend, proposed by the board, compares to 2.33 crowns paid the year before, Perstorp said.
Operating income totalled 12.93 billion crowns compared to 13.00 billion. Operating expenses fell marginally to 11.44 billion crowns from 11.56 billion.
The division Perstorp Surface Materials contributed the most to operating revenue, accounting for 2.46 billion crowns compared to 2.48 billion the year before.
"The business area was mainly affected by the very weak conditions in the European construction industry," the company said.
